lead: Induction of labour starts labour artificially before it begins on its own, aiming at vaginal birth. It differs from augmentation, which speeds up labour that has already started. The Bishop score decides whether the cervix must be ripened first.
f: Prolonged pregnancy (commonest) · PROM at term · Pre-eclampsia, eclampsia · Unexplained APH at term · Chorioamnionitis · FGR, oligohydramnios, abnormal Doppler · IUFD · Rh isoimmunisation · Severe hypertension, uncontrolled diabetes, renal disease, cholestasis

sc: Labour already started, slow → Augmentation, not induction

f: Absolute: placenta or vasa praevia, transverse or oblique lie, cord presentation or prolapse, CPD, classical CS, 2 or more CS, previous rupture, active herpes, VVF repair · Relative: one previous lower-segment CS, breech, high free head, grand multipara, polyhydramnios, twins, heart disease, asthma (prostaglandins) · Before inducing: clear indication, sure dates, lie and pelvis checked, normal CTG

Five items: consistency, position, effacement (cervical length), dilatation, station · Each 0–3 (consistency and position 0–2), maximum 13 · 8 or more: favourable → ARM + oxytocin · 6 or less: unfavourable → ripen first · Success also depends on gestation and parity (multipara better)

sc: Cervix 3 cm, 1.5 cm long, soft, mid, station −1 → Bishop 9: favourable

f: Membrane sweep at 40–41 wk · Dinoprostone 3 mg PV, repeat after 6 h, max 2 doses: the live fetus · Misoprostol: live term fetus 25 µg PV 6-hourly or 25 µg oral 2-hourly (WHO 2022 prefers oral); IUFD dose by weeks; never in a scarred uterus · Foley balloon 30–50 mL, 12–24 h: no hyperstimulation, choice after a previous CS · ARM with the head fixed; check liquor and cord · Oxytocin after ARM, at least 6 h after the last prostaglandin

sc: Prostin 2 h ago, no labour → Wait 6 h before oxytocin

f: 5 IU in 500 mL saline = 10 mU/mL · Start 2 mU/min (4 drops) · Increase 2–4 mU/min every 30 min · Aim 3–4 contractions in 10 min, 40–60 s each · Maximum 32 mU/min · Saline, not large volumes of dextrose (water intoxication)

sc: 18 h of oxytocin with 3 L of 5% dextrose, now confused and fitting → Water intoxication (hyponatraemia)

f: Drugs: hyperstimulation → fetal distress, uterine rupture; water intoxication · ARM: cord prolapse (high head), infection, abruption (polyhydramnios) · Any IOL: failed induction, prematurity, PPH, instrumental birth · Tachysystole: over 5 contractions in 10 min; hypertonus: one over 2 min; hyperstimulation = either + abnormal FHR · Stop oxytocin, left lateral, fluids, terbutaline 0.25 mg SC; restart lower after 30 min; persistent bradycardia → CS

sc: On oxytocin, 6 in 10 min, FHR 80 → Stop it, terbutaline

f: Failed: no labour after a full course (2 prostins or Foley, then ARM + oxytocin 6–12 h) → rest and second course, or CS · One lower-segment CS: hospital with theatre; Foley + ARM + oxytocin; prostin lowest dose; no misoprostol with a live fetus; continuous CTG · Rupture risk about 0.5% in spontaneous labour, 2–3 times higher if induced · Classical scar, 2 or more CS, previous rupture: elective CS

tr: Scar rupture often shows first as fetal bradycardia, not pain
sc: One previous CS, 41+3 wk, Bishop 3 → Foley balloon, then ARM + oxytocin
